# Results — Study 353 (Smart-Money-Concepts: ICT order blocks & fair-value gaps)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The viral "ICT / Smart Money
Concepts" claim — that price leaves institutional **footprints** and "respects order blocks"
and "fills fair-value gaps" — tested on a real SPY daily tape against the proper null: a
matched random walk, which **also** produces gaps and bounces. Offline, deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | SPY daily OHLC (yfinance public download, no key) |
| Window | 1993-01-29 → **2026-06-18** (8,404 daily bars) · **as-of 2026-06-18** |
| SPY range | \$43 – \$760 · daily return σ = 0.0117 |
| Content fingerprint | `sha256[:12] = ed7e466d0523` (over rounded OHLC) |
| Null / control | deterministic driftless random-walk OHLC, seed 353, σ matched to the tape |

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* — one instrument (SPY), one daily
> resolution, one 33-year window; the FVG/OB *definitions* are the common YouTube ones
> (other ICT variants exist, but the geometry argument is definition-agnostic). *Tradability*
> — the OB book never clears a t of 2, so no realistic cost is needed to kill it; we charge
> costs anyway to show it only gets worse. The synthetic control is a **machinery proof**
> (the detector fires on noise), never market evidence.

## Claim (a) — fair-value gaps fill no better than random zones (MIRAGE of a footprint)

A 3-bar FVG: a *bullish* gap is a bar whose low sits above the high two bars back (an untouched
void below price); *bearish* is the mirror. SPY carries **2,337** such gaps (1,423 bull, 914
bear; median width 0.53% of price). "Fill" = a later bar's range touches back into the void.
We compare the real fill-rate to a within-tape **placebo** (a same-width zone at a random bar)
and to the **random-walk synthetic**:

| horizon (bars) | real FVG fill | placebo random zone | random-walk synth | z (real − placebo) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5  | 71.8% | 74.0% | 70.5% | **−1.71** |
| 10 | 79.1% | 80.5% | 77.9% | **−1.20** |
| 20 | 84.2% | 86.4% | 83.6% | **−2.15** |
| 40 | 88.7% | 88.8% | 88.2% | **−0.05** |

Median time-to-fill among filled gaps: **1 bar**. At every horizon the real fill-rate is
**indistinguishable from, or marginally *below*,** the placebo and the random walk — the
real-minus-placebo z is at best negative. An 84% fill-rate sounds like a respected level; it is
just what *any* same-size void near a noisy price does. **The footprint is geometry, not smart
money.**

## Claim (b) — order-block forward returns do not beat random levels (NONE)

A *bullish* order block = the last down-candle before a ≥1.5% three-bar up-impulse; we enter in
the OB's direction at the bar **after** price first revisits the zone (one-bar execution lag)
and hold 10 bars. SPY carries **1,440** OBs (787 bull, 653 bear).

| book | n | mean fwd 10-bar return | t vs 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| OB revisit (signed) | 1,403 | **−0.114%** | −1.04 |
| random-entry control (signed) | 28,060 | −0.027% | −1.41 |
| **Welch OB − random** | — | **−0.087%** | **t = −0.78 (p = 0.435)** |
| random-walk synthetic OB | 1,896 | −0.061% | −0.72 |

The OB book's forward return is **slightly negative and statistically zero**; the difference vs
random entry is insignificant (t = −0.78). Charging one-way costs (entry + exit) only deepens
the hole: net of 5 bp/leg the mean is −0.214% (t = −1.96, the wrong sign). The random walk
produces an equally-good "edge" (t = −0.72). **No edge to harvest.**

## Positive control — a random walk leaves the same footprints

On a driftless random-walk tape (seed 353, σ matched to SPY) the detector finds **2,900** FVGs
that fill **83.6%** of the time at H=20, and **1,933** order blocks whose forward "edge" is
t = −0.72 (noise). The patterns the meme calls institutional fingerprints are reproduced, in
the same abundance, by a process with **no institutions and no memory**. This is the control the
ICT claim has to beat — and the real tape does not beat it.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** FVG fill-rate does not exceed a matched random zone at any horizon
  (real − placebo z ≤ 0; e.g. −2.15 at H=20), and OB forward returns are statistically zero
  and indistinguishable from random entry (Welch t = −0.78). The headline 84% fill-rate is
  geometry; both effects are fully reproduced on a memory-less random walk. No robust t ≥ 2 in
  the *direction the claim predicts* anywhere.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** With the underlying signal already absent gross, costs are
  academic: the OB book is negative gross (−0.11%) and more negative after the 2-leg spread
  (−0.21% at 5 bp/leg). Nothing to scale.
- **Footprints? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The synthetic positive control fires identically on pure
  noise, so an order block or a fair-value gap is **not** evidence of "smart money" — it is the
  expected geometry of any random walk.

> **One sentence.** ICT "Smart Money Concepts" describes real chart shapes — gaps and bounces —
> that a coin-flip random walk produces just as often, fill just as fast, and reverse no
> differently, so there is no measurable footprint and nothing to trade.
